requirements.text: Please create a leave request case with a description noting the upcoming medical leave under Leave Of Absence service.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 6 AND opened_for = 5 AND opened_by = 5 AND account_number = 'ACC-242-657' AND short_description LIKE 'Service: %, Subject: %, Detail: %' AND short_description LIKE '%medical%' AND priority = 'moderate' AND coe_type = 'Total Rewards'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id on the seed is 60); it is the only case the request creates
Leave Of Absence is hr_service 6 (active); Mckenzie Mendez is user 5 with hr_profile 5
opened_by 5: the policy defines opened_by as the requester, Mckenzie Mendez sent the request, and all 60 seed cases, whatever their source, have opened_by equal to opened_for
account_number from the request's 'Ac No: ACC-242-657'
short_description follows the policy's case format 'Service: <>, Subject: <>, Detail: <>.' as the benchmark tests, and must note the medical leave, as the request asks
priority not stated; the policy's default is moderate
coe_type Total Rewards: the service's topic detail (Leave of Absence) lies under the Benefits category, coe_type Total Rewards, as on the seed's Leave Of Absence cases

disagreement: opened_by: A 5, B untested; chose 5 because the policy names the requester as opened_by, the request says Mckenzie Mendez sent the request, and every seed case has opened_by equal to opened_for

requirements.text: Assign the case to Joanne Simpson
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND assigned_to = 4 AND status = 'awaiting_acceptance' AND request_status = 'requested'
assumptions: Joanne Simpson is user 4 (active manager, the only user of that name)
status awaiting_acceptance and request_status requested: the policy requires them upon assigning a case to a user or group, overriding the default ready

requirements.text: make sure the HR Service Desk is reviewing it as well
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND assignment_group = 4
assumptions: HR Service Desk is user_group 4; 'reviewing it' read as the case's assignment group

requirements.text: Assign the case to Joanne Simpson and make sure the HR Service Desk is reviewing it as well
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 4 AND user_id = 4
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id on the seed is 43); it is the only membership the request creates
required by the policy, not stated in the request: the assignee must be an active user in the assignment group and is added to it if not a member; Joanne Simpson belongs only to group 10 on the seed

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's opened_by: one pass tests 5 (Mckenzie Mendez), the other leaves it untested as possibly the acting user; kept 5, because the policy names the requester as opened_by, the request says Mckenzie Mendez sent the request, and all 60 seed cases have opened_by equal to opened_for.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition: case 61 for user 5 on service 6, assigned to user 4 in group 4, and membership 44 adding user 4 to group 4.
The case is the only hr_case row created, so it is anchored at the next id and its cells are split by the request's three asks (create, assign to Joanne Simpson, HR Service Desk); all three carry the benchmark's case check, which does not test the assignee.
The acting user, Karen Watkins (user 39), is an admin, and the policy says an admin must not perform routine HR case work; the request asks for the case, so it is required.
The policy's default status for a new case is ready and its lifecycle lists no direct ready to awaiting_acceptance transition, but section 3.2 requires awaiting_acceptance with request_status requested once a case is assigned; the requirements follow section 3.2, as the benchmark does.
The case's source is not tested: 'sent a message' fits email or chat, and the policy sets no default; nor is account_type, which the request does not state.
The description's Service, Subject and Detail slots are not tested beyond the format the benchmark checks and the mention of medical leave; the policy's 30-120 character limit on short_description is not tested, as the benchmark does not test it.
The membership row's organisation is not tested; HR Service Desk and Joanne Simpson both belong to organisation 1.
